selection: Analytic preselection, not a new statistical experiment; old anchors chosen because their multiple distinct doublets were already established.
reason: Every nonempty absolute SET patch is idempotent on its record state. A second identical group cannot be canonical after the first, so only the globally unique REPEAT form may double. Each reader already has both ol/ol and daiin/daiin inside definite same-line spans.
assumptions: Exactly one whole canonical patch or one globally fixed REPEAT per whole group.
Only truly changed fields emitted, state-independent injective patch serialization.
No reset inside the selected ordinary definite spaces; reset only at explicitly visible paragraph start.
Alternate readings are not independent evidence.
scope_limits: No native value is assigned to either repeated form.
GDT1005 allows two records per group, so its full contract is not refuted by this one-patch lemma.
Redundant SETs, multiple REPEAT spellings, relative increments and state-dependent code values lie outside this contract.
No new image or paleographic reset verification; conditional on retained transcriptions and the stated paragraph-reset model.
No source-frequency test, GDT388 relation score, significance or general contextual-writing rejection.
decision: Do not build a renderer for the stipulated one-patch contract. Retain older model failures unchanged; no automatic relative-delta or alias repair.
proof_review: Producer supplied algebraic argument; root independently read contract and prior primaries, checked T(T(s))=T(s), and revalidated the already known source anchors. No independent native observation or semantic confirmation.
